scope: Exact retained native source packages as of 15 October 2026. Original accepted packages are retained except for explicit Z-Anatomy expansion and six additional source configurations. Counts are source-specific entries, not unique anatomy or a completeness percentage. Independent anatomical review is separate.

course_plans.title: BigBrain cortical layers and hippocampal subfields
course_plans.objective: Study histology-derived cortical boundary and hippocampal source surfaces in their preserved native packages. Compare source definitions and observe folding without introducing a cross-atlas registration.

course_plans.title: Cisternal regions: native image and spatial observation
course_plans.objective: Use source MRI, surrounding labelled anatomy and explicit teaching annotations to discuss cisternal regional relationships. Inspect the supplied T2 image in its independent native space.

course_plans.title: Cranial nerves: source objects and regional context
course_plans.objective: Inspect source-model nerve objects and roots, categorical tissue classes, supplied trajectories and brainstem source regions. Compare these independent representations with their stated source definitions.

course_plans.title: Association and limbic white matter probability anatomy
course_plans.objective: Explore all 64 source probability fields and their corresponding original T1/T2 template samples. Follow association, limbic, projection and callosal subdivisions, with explicit probability and display-mask comparisons.

course_plans.title: Projection and callosal white matter probability anatomy
course_plans.objective: Explore all 64 source probability fields and their corresponding original T1/T2 template samples. Follow association, limbic, projection and callosal subdivisions, with explicit probability and display-mask comparisons.

course_plans.title: Brainstem nuclei, root assignments and cranial-nerve context
course_plans.objective: Explore supplied cranial-nerve components, auditory and vestibular nuclei, selected midbrain and pontine nuclei, and lower cranial nuclear relationships. Each recorded view retains its source definitions and independent native coordinate frame.

course_plans.title: Cerebellar surfaces, lobular fields and deep nuclei
course_plans.objective: Compare the supplied cerebellar surface model, original SUIT lobular and nuclear fields, and individual reconstructed cerebellar tissue labels. Each recorded view retains its source definitions and independent native coordinate frame.

course_plans.title: Cortical folds, cytoarchitectonic assignments and layer boundaries
course_plans.objective: Explore central cortical surface objects, source cytoarchitectonic population assignments and reconstructed cortical layer-boundary sheets. Each recorded view retains its source definitions and independent native coordinate frame.

course_plans.title: Hippocampal layers, subfields and white-matter context
course_plans.objective: Compare source-defined CA1 layers, dentate and CA4 regions, subiculum, midsurface and fornix-related context across original block reconstruction, surfaces and population fields. Each recorded view retains its source definitions and independent native coordinate frame.

course_plans.title: Intracranial anatomy: first teaching session
course_plans.objective: Identify source-labelled cortex, deep structures, ventricular spaces, brainstem and cerebellum in linked native MRI and 3D views.

course_plans.title: NextBrain Case 1: histological fine anatomy and MRI
course_plans.objective: Explore hippocampal layers, amygdalar regions, thalamic nuclei, hypothalamic and basal forebrain subdivisions, and deep cerebellar nuclei in source-preserving native tissue blocks. Each block keeps its supplied grid and extent.

course_plans.title: NextBrain Case 2: brainstem fine anatomy and MRI
course_plans.objective: Explore source-defined brainstem nuclei, cranial roots, fibre crossings and tract assignments in four original histological blocks with matching ex vivo MRI. Move from midbrain through pons to medulla while preserving each block extent.

course_plans.title: Interpreting normal variation across individual and population sources
course_plans.objective: Use original volunteer MRA, arterial occurrence, venous field dispersion, cerebellar assignment and observer support to distinguish the types of evidence used when discussing normal anatomical variation. Compare independent sources without coordinate transfer or unsupported named-variant diagnosis.

course_plans.title: Regional anatomy across native source atlases
course_plans.objective: Observe source definitions of cortical, deep, ventricular, brainstem and cerebellar regions. Compare recorded views while retaining each source native space and evidence type.

course_plans.title: Skull base: source skull, dura and intracranial context
course_plans.objective: Observe original skull surfaces, source dural objects and surrounding categorical anatomy. Use reversible display cuts and independently inspect the corresponding skull mask sections.

course_plans.title: Cerebellar lobules, vermis and deep nuclei
course_plans.objective: Explore all 34 source compartments in original SUIT coordinates, compare categorical surfaces with population probability fields and locate them in the matching T1 template.

course_plans.title: Cerebral arterial segments in healthy volunteer MRA
course_plans.objective: Follow actual MRA signal and original categorical segments within three healthy-volunteer source cases. Compare anterior, posterior and carotid segment courses and the case-specific extent of annotation. Each case retains its own source coordinate frame.

course_plans.title: Normal arterial variation: source observations across eight volunteers
course_plans.objective: Compare anterior and posterior arterial courses in eight original healthy-volunteer MRA cases. Record observed image signal, source annotation coverage and unresolved interpretation separately. Each case retains its native author-processed coordinates. These selected examples are not a prevalence sample and do not establish named vascular variants.

course_plans.title: Vascular anatomy: native images, fields and source models
course_plans.objective: Observe vascular signal, arterial occurrence, venous statistical fields and named anatomical source models in their own spaces. Explain the evidence represented by each view.

course_plans.title: White matter: supplied streamline pathways
course_plans.objective: Inspect association, projection, commissural, cerebellar and source-named cranial pathways with their reference MRI. Retain source trajectory vertices and display sampling records.

course_plans.title: Cerebellar and ventricular source-model relationships
course_plans.objective: Explore the original model surfaces of cerebellar lobules, vermis, peduncular context, ventricles, aqueduct and choroid plexus.

course_plans.title: Frontal and central cortical surface relationships
course_plans.objective: Explore original frontal, central, temporal, parietal, insular, medial and basal cortical surface objects within their source-model hemispheres.

course_plans.title: Medial and basal cortical surface relationships
course_plans.objective: Explore original frontal, central, temporal, parietal, insular, medial and basal cortical surface objects within their source-model hemispheres.

course_plans.title: Temporal, parietal and insular surface relationships
course_plans.objective: Explore original frontal, central, temporal, parietal, insular, medial and basal cortical surface objects within their source-model hemispheres.

course_plans.title: Source models: distal arteries, sensory pathways and petrous context
course_plans.objective: Explore named distal arterial branches, separate visual and auditory neural components, and petrous inner-ear relationships in one original source model.

course_plans.title: Sella, clinoid processes and sphenoidal grooves
course_plans.objective: Locate nine original author annotations in the source sphenoid model. Compare complete bone context with focused views of the sella, clinoid processes and adjacent grooves, retaining the original source locations and model geometry.
